history.name: Nutritional_Label_Expert
history.content: Task kickoff: We need to compare the butterfat content listed on the pint to the US federal standard (Wikipedia 2020) and report the percent above/below. Plan: 1) Extract butterfat/milk fat percentage from the image. 2) Confirm federal standard. 3) Compute percent difference relative to the standard and round to one decimal with sign. I will start with OCR to read the label text.

history.name: USDA_Food_Standards_Expert
history.content: Federal Standard Reference: In the United States, ice cream must contain at least 10% milk fat (butterfat) by weight. Wikipedia (as of 2020) reflects this standard: 10% minimum butterfat. Once we have the pint's butterfat percentage, I will calculate the percent difference: ((pint_butterfat - 10) / 10) * 100.

history.content: Calculation with assumed butterfat = 14%: Percent difference relative to 10% standard = ((14 - 10) / 10) * 100 = 40%. Rounded to one decimal: +40.0. Preliminary result: +40.0.

mistake_reason: The Nutritional_Label_Expert incorrectly interpreted OCR output text "Total Fat 14g 18%" as indicating a 14% milk fat (butterfat) content for the ice cream. The tool output clearly denotes total fat per serving (grams) alongside % Daily Value, not butterfat percentage. This misinterpretation of the tool’s output (treating '14g' as '14%' milk fat) led to using 14% as the butterfat value and ultimately computing a +40.0% difference, which is incorrect. This aligns with FM-4.2: Tool Output Misinterpretation.
